lead: This part turns the record into work. Fifteen packages cover every bottleneck in the register and every idea that is still live. Each card says what the package is for, where it works, its first deliverable, how we will know it is done and what it waits on. Six can start today, six start the day I give my word, and three follow another package. Before you take one, read the box under the map: it holds the few rules that keep two people, two projects and one PC from getting in each other’s way.
mapShows: The left column needs no decision from me, no agents and no Docker gate for its first deliverable, so it can start today. The middle column waits on a word from me, and the right column on another package.
decLead: Every open decision that holds up a package, in one place. Bold marks the option the source design recommends; where nothing is bold, there is no recommendation yet. I answered D01 to D06 on 11 November: yes to phase 1, an encrypted external drive for the copy, Docker’s start at sign-in stays off for now, no sleep on mains power, a sensor logger and a debugger are allowed, and sessions come back from a resume list two at a time.
before: Each card says whether it works in FixFlow (this repository) or in the clinic testbed. Work on a branch, never on main. The ship plan and this compile live on the plan branch (PR #182), the knowledge-store design on PR #183’s branch and the skills on PR #185’s branch.

Before you use the Docker gate or start an agent, look at the lane board in `W0-results.md`. If a FixFlow phase is running or waiting on its reviewer, harness work that needs the gate or agents waits.
One budget for the whole team

The two-lane cap and the written token budget (D07) are shared by all of us, not per person. Book agent runs in the one queue on the decision board and launch nothing on your own. The cap is for harness work; FixFlow’s lanes follow the ship plan’s own rule.
Both projects share this PC’s 31 GB [M] of memory, so a heavy check from either one counts against one shared limit. Leave the three slots of FixFlow’s `ff-slot.sh` as they are.
The coordinator writes FixFlow’s program files
A package that would change the ship plan, the lane board or FixFlow’s gate scripts sends a proposal. The coordinator decides and writes it.
Machine traps that already cost us time

Never prune Docker networks or restart Docker: other sessions run containers. Anything that needs its own Docker network gets an explicit subnet inside 10.77.0.0/16. With `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV` set, write paths as `C:/…`. Clone into scratch folders with `core.longpaths` on. There is no `python` on PATH; our scripts run with Node. Never touch the antivirus.

packages.name: Machine and recovery
packages.mapLine: Copy off the PC, resume list, always-on logger
packages.worksIn: This PC and the clinic testbed repository; scripts and settings only, on a branch.
packages.goal: No power-off costs us work or a day. The work is copied off the PC every night, sessions come back from a resume list, and an always-on logger finally tells us why the PC powers off. This is harness v2 phase 1.
packages.first: Today: the bundle-and-verify script and the nightly copy script. They must also capture the six [M] folders that are in no commit and the untracked harness documents. After I plug in and encrypt the drive, which comes after FixFlow’s P0a: the first verified copy.
packages.firstShort: Bundle-and-verify and nightly copy scripts; first verified copy after my drive step
packages.done: A clone from the copy shows the same heads, and the copy is never more than 24 hours old [T]. After one real reboot the resume list appears at sign-in with “start Docker” as its first line, and once Docker is up the databases in use are healthy within 3 minutes [T] with no further command. The next unexpected shutdown leaves a logger trace that ends at it.
packages.skills: Windows administration, PowerShell or bash scripting, git.
packages.size: One to two days of one session [E], scripts and settings only, no agents.
packages.depText: Needs nothing from another package. Mechanisms 7 and 8 (one fact, one command; a session parks itself when its record and branch disagree) come in here, because they cost one line in a brief.
packages.mine: Switch off sleep on mains power (D04); plug in the drive and switch on its encryption (D02); install the sensor logger and debugger (D05); write down the days the house lost power; say yes to the nightly copy as a scheduled task and to permission rules that deny agents `railway up` and `railway run`; later, D08 (a battery backup) once the diagnosis is in. My steps come after FixFlow’s P0a.

packages.name: The clinic check
packages.mapLine: Container gate, slots from one number, heartbeat
packages.goal: One fast, fair and visible check for the clinic testbed: the Linux container run as the gate, check slots sized from one measured memory number, a queue that prints each check’s place, a heartbeat while it runs, and a reaper that lists what can be cleaned up. This is harness v2 phase 2.
packages.first: The container run and the Windows run side by side on recorded commits, with one check’s peak memory written down [M]. I decide D09 on that evidence.
packages.firstShort: Container and Windows runs side by side; one check’s peak memory written down
packages.done: Median gate near 230 s [T], zero Linux-only failures on main, no gap between heartbeats longer than 60 s [T], the next stall names its test, and after each merge the worktree and container counts return to the active slices plus one.
packages.skills: Docker and Linux, test runners (pytest, Vitest, Jest), queues.
packages.size: Three to four days of one session [E], including one observed build day for the memory table. No agents.
packages.depText: The side-by-side runs need only a quiet machine. The memory table and any second slot need WP1’s logger and diagnosis first. The reaper only lists until I decide D10, and never touches a container, network or worktree it did not create.
packages.mine: D09 (the container run as the gate), D10 (what may be cleaned up), and later D11 (who gives up memory).

packages.name: FixFlow’s gate harness and CI checks
packages.mapLine: Per-lane gates, fair slots, CI that can fail
packages.worksIn: FixFlow (this repository). Ship lanes use these scripts every day, so each change goes to the coordinator as a proposal and lands by atomic rename.
packages.goal: Keep FixFlow’s own gates fast, fair and honest: the per-lane gate harness and slot lock the ship lanes use, a gate that mirrors CI, and CI checks that fail when they should and never pass a run that tested nothing.
packages.first: Gate waits measured per lane under the new ticket queue, and a negative run proving the CI checks fail when they should: skipped integration tests fail the job, and Jest never runs with `--passWithNoTests`.
packages.firstShort: Gate waits per lane measured; a negative run proving CI fails when it should
packages.done: Every gate kind takes the per-lane lock first, Node failures are re-run under Node 22 before they are called defects, and a planted skip or an empty test run turns CI red.
packages.skills: Bash, Docker, GitHub Actions, pytest and Jest.
packages.size: A day or two per item [G]. The changes are small; the care is in not disturbing running lanes.
packages.depText: Needs nothing from another package. It starts on my word because the coordinator owns these scripts while ship lanes run.
packages.mine: My go, through the coordinator, before any change to `ff-gates.sh` or `ff-slot.sh`.

packages.name: Gate, review and merge scripts
packages.mapLine: Sealed replay, transcript audit, merge queue
packages.worksIn: The clinic testbed’s recorded history, read only, and a scripts folder on a branch. Changes to FixFlow’s review practice are proposals to the coordinator.
packages.goal: Move the mechanical part of review and merging out of the orchestrating session into scripts that spend no tokens: a sealed replay, a verdict script, a transcript audit at merge, one finding table, a dry run with stand-in agents and a merge queue that checks who read the final commit. Then the fix-round contract. This is harness v2 phase 3.
packages.first: The sealed replay and the transcript audit (mechanisms 1 and 3). Both cost no tokens and no check time, so they can start today on the recorded data.
packages.firstShort: Sealed replay and transcript audit, on the record
packages.done: Each of the six scripts passes its stated test, and the merge queue has run record-only over the 65 [M] recorded merges and flagged the unread final heads of 10 and 11 November by itself. A script refuses a merge only after I say so (D15).
packages.skills: Scripting, git internals, test tooling, careful diff reading.
packages.size: About a week of one session for the scripts [E].
packages.depText: The verdict script re-runs the cited tests, which takes check time, so it is easier after WP2a and runs only in a quiet window. The fix-round contract comes after the seal and the verdict script.
packages.mine: D12 to D20, each as its mechanism reaches me. D13 (one reports folder) and D17 (hooks) are permission changes.

packages.name: Planner and lanes
packages.mapLine: Lane count below the knee, no file collisions
packages.worksIn: Reads FixFlow’s ship plan §7 and its lane board and never edits them. Its output is a recommendation the coordinator may adopt.
packages.goal: Know before a wave starts which slices can run side by side, how many lanes are worth it and where they would collide: the planner, the scheduler and the plan check of harness v2, measured against how FixFlow already runs its lanes.
packages.first: The plan check replayed on FixFlow’s first lane wave, whose lanes declared the files they own (ship plan §7.3): the collision graph and the lane count it would have chosen.
packages.firstShort: Plan check replayed on FixFlow’s first lane wave
packages.done: It runs record-only on the next wave first, and sets the lane count only after the coordinator and I accept it.
packages.skills: Graphs and scheduling, scripting, a feel for queues.
packages.depText: Needs WP8’s rate sheet first: the planner reads its rates from there. Easier after WP2a, because check capacity is one of the limits it plans against.
packages.mine: Accepting its recommendation, together with the coordinator.

packages.name: Token budget
packages.mapLine: Written budget per window; the four levers
packages.worksIn: Transcripts on this PC, read only, and Claude Code settings, for both projects.
packages.goal: Give every wave a written token budget and put the four levers from the token report to work: cap long windows, shrink the fixed start every agent re-reads, batch lookups, and stop the model’s own output piling up in its window.
packages.first: A proposal for D07, the token budget per window, built at zero tokens from the saved November baseline. Lever 2 is measured once D07 is set and no FixFlow phase is running.
packages.firstShort: D07 budget proposal from the saved baseline
packages.done: Every wave launches with a written budget and books its agents in the shared queue, each lever has a before-and-after number, and the compaction-window trial is reported as an anecdote. No lever claims fewer stops, because how re-reads count against the limit is still unknown to us.
packages.skills: Data analysis on transcripts (JSON), Claude Code settings.
packages.size: About an hour for the proposal [E]; a day or two per lever [G].
packages.depText: Needs nothing to start. Levers 2 and 3 are measured after WP3’s gate workflow and short tool list, because those change what a session costs.
packages.mine: D07 (the budget per window), D22 (the compaction-window trial), and my yes before connectors or tool descriptions are removed from agent sessions, which is a settings change.

packages.name: The library and lesson memory
packages.mapLine: Limitations first, then a held-out pilot
packages.worksIn: Design documents and the clinic testbed’s recorded runs. Nothing is built until the limitation list is agreed.
packages.goal: Give the harness a memory a cheaper model can use: the reasoning-cache library of harness v2, written when something becomes true and asked for, never pushed. We agree what can go wrong before we choose any fix.
packages.first: The library’s limitation list agreed with me, with the pathway map’s two weights for each limitation (alone, and as the last one left).
packages.done: A pilot on held-out work measures whether a session that asks the library first reads less and gets more right, under the frozen validation contract.
packages.skills: Information retrieval, evaluation design, a feel for how models use context.
packages.size: Not sized yet [G]; the list itself is a conversation and a document.
packages.depText: The pilot needs WP8’s frozen validation contract and pre-registered protocol first, spends agents only under D07 and books its place in the shared queue.

packages.name: The knowledge store (PR #183)
packages.mapLine: Free recurrence audit, then my second yes
packages.worksIn: FixFlow’s history, read only, for the audit; the design on PR #183’s branch. Its phases always yield to ship phases.
packages.goal: Build, if the audit says it would pay, the knowledge store designed in PR #183: a store of hard solved problems, traps and do-not-apply facts, looked up by pull only, and stale when its code changes, never by age.
packages.first: The free recurrence audit (KS-0): one Sonnet session and an Opus refuter count the repeats a store could have served. No code is written.
packages.done: The audit has reported. If I then say yes to a build (KS-D1b), the pilot (KS-5) meets the design’s go marks: recall at shown of 60 % or more [T], zero acted-on false positives [T], and every planted forbidden diff caught [T].
packages.size: The audit: one session [E]. A build is sized only after the audit.
packages.depText: Never displaces a ship phase. Any pilot needs WP8’s frozen validation contract first.
packages.mine: KS-D1 (run the audit), KS-D1b (build after the audit), and my yes before any copy of the store leaves this PC.

packages.name: Docs that stay true to the code
packages.mapLine: CI checks on stated facts; one corrections PR
packages.goal: Make our documents fail a check when they drift from the code: a CI check that the facts CLAUDE.md states still match the code, prose contradictions turned into one corrections PR, and memory files that point to the truth instead of restating it.
packages.first: A CI check for the Alembic head number that CLAUDE.md states, and one corrections PR that settles each known contradiction against git.
packages.firstShort: Alembic-head CI check; one corrections PR
packages.done: A planted wrong fact in CLAUDE.md turns CI red, and the corrections PR has merged.
packages.skills: CI (GitHub Actions), careful reading, technical writing.
packages.depText: Needs nothing from another package. It lands through the coordinator, after the ship phase in flight.
packages.mine: My go through the coordinator, and the merge.

packages.name: Retrieval and graphs
packages.mapLine: Index replay at zero tokens, then an agent
packages.worksIn: FixFlow’s history and the graph-test evidence. Engines run in one Linux image.
packages.goal: Give sessions a fast, trustworthy answer to “what does this change touch?”: the typed code store, the touch list and indexes, and the wider test of knowledge graphs, time and caching that I asked for.
packages.first: The index replay at zero tokens on the recorded windows, once D23 sets what it must show.
packages.done: A tested answer to whether an agent with the typed store finds what a change touches faster and with fewer tokens than the same agent with search alone.
packages.skills: Static analysis, graph databases, evaluation statistics.
packages.size: The replay: a few days of one session [G]. The agent arm is sized from the replay.
packages.depText: The agent arm needs WP8’s pre-registered protocol, the index replay’s result, D07 and a quiet window, and books its agents in the shared queue.
packages.mine: D23 (what the index replay must show), the agent pilot, and each install when its arm is scheduled: a graph database server, graphify, an embedding model.

packages.name: Measurement and fair tests
packages.mapLine: Rate sheet, frozen contract, fair-test rules
packages.worksIn: The record on this PC, read only. Results go into the repository as evidence.
packages.goal: Keep the numbers every package depends on, and the rules that keep our tests fair: token tallies, check and review rates, the system-dynamics model, the frozen validation contract and the pre-registered protocols.
packages.first: A rate sheet from the record: check run time, review rounds, the share of reviews that sent work back and limit episodes, each with its tag. What the record cannot supply yet, peak memory per check and lane collisions, is written as unknown, never as zero.
packages.firstShort: Rate sheet from the record, unknowns marked
packages.done: Every package’s “done when” has a measured before and after, and the planner and the governor read their rates from the sheet.
packages.skills: Statistics, simulation (Monte Carlo), JavaScript or Python.
packages.size: About a day for the rate sheet [G]; no wait on me, zero tokens.
packages.depText: Needs nothing. WP4, WP6a, WP6b and WP7 need its contract and protocols.

packages.name: First use and real hosts
packages.mapLine: Zero-seed walk in the gate; real-host rehearsal
packages.worksIn: The clinic testbed repository. FixFlow’s device lab and Android builds belong to the ship plan’s lab (§7); this package only reads them.
packages.goal: Find the last-day gaps on day one: a zero-seed walk in every gate, a rehearsal on a real host, and a load rerun. This is harness v2 phase 4.
packages.first: The zero-seed walk as a step of the container gate: install, first user, tills and accounts, a real-shaped import, one transaction and the close of day, on a fresh database.
packages.firstShort: Zero-seed walk as a gate step
packages.done: The walk fails on the commit before the 11 November merge and passes after it [T], and the first-deploy checklist has run once on a real host.
packages.size: Two to three days of one session [E].
packages.depText: Needs WP2a’s container gate first: the walk runs inside it.
packages.mine: D21 (rehearse on a real host). The rig steps need me present for one administrator prompt, and a rented host costs a domain fee and a few hours of rental and takes made-up data off this PC, so it waits for my yes.

packages.name: Briefs, workflows and review method
packages.worksIn: How every session in both projects is briefed. Changes to FixFlow’s ship plan or lane board are proposals to the coordinator.
packages.goal: Brief and run agents well: the brief contract and return schemas, discovery without judgement and with citations, fresh-context skeptics and refuters, saved workflows, and the rules that keep a session’s state on disk.
packages.first: The save-as-run rule adopted, and one saved review-stage script committed, now that FixFlow’s P1 has merged.
packages.firstShort: Save-as-run rule; one saved review-stage script
packages.done: Every workflow we run is saved and can be re-run, raw workflow outputs are committed as evidence with a hash manifest, and a brief edit that flips a recorded verdict is caught by a frozen replay.
packages.skills: Prompt writing, workflow scripting, Claude Code.
packages.depText: Needs nothing to start. Anything that launches agents waits for D07.

packages.name: Skills and agents (PR #185)
packages.goal: Give agents tested domain skills: the 13 skill packages and 11 FixFlow agents of PR #185, each with a pinned model, a short tool list and a small fixed start.
packages.first: PR #185 reviewed and merged with its stray artifact removed, and a CI check for skill and agent frontmatter (the settings block at the top of each file).
packages.firstShort: PR #185 reviewed and merged; frontmatter CI check
packages.done: A trigger tally over six phases shows which skills fire, and lookups run on the pinned cheaper agents, with their token use compared against the built-in agent’s.
packages.skills: Prompt writing, Claude Code configuration, domain knowledge (Android, Odoo, accounting).
packages.size: Two to three days [G] for the review and the CI check.
packages.depText: The binding review spends an Opus agent, so it runs under D07 when no FixFlow phase is waiting on its reviewer. Each agent’s fixed start is measured once, by WP5’s lever 2.
packages.mine: Merging PR #185, and deleting its stray artifact.

packages.name: Decisions and the pages I read
packages.mapLine: One decision board; pages I can read
packages.worksIn: My visual pages and the program documents on the plan branch. Ship-plan items are linked, never owned.
packages.goal: Keep me deciding quickly and seeing clearly: one board for every open decision, visual pages I can read on my own screen, and this compile kept current.
packages.first: One decision board that joins harness D01 to D23, the knowledge store’s KS-D decisions, the graph-test decisions and the FixFlow items of mine that the harness touches, each with a distinct prefix and what it unblocks.
packages.done: No package waits more than a day [T] on a decision of mine, with each wait logged.
packages.skills: Front-end and data visualisation, clear writing.
packages.size: About a day for the board [G].
packages.depText: Needs nothing; every package feeds it.
packages.mine: Answering the board. “Accept all defaults” covers only decisions that stay on this PC and spend no money; installs, hooks, permissions, scheduled tasks, deletes, a rented host and anything that leaves this PC each keep their own yes.

decisions.q: FixFlow’s P0a, my own steps in the ship plan
decisions.options: **Do P0a first; my harness steps follow it**

decisions.q: The power-cut notes
decisions.when: now (the rest of D05 is answered)
decisions.options: **Write down the days the house lost power**

decisions.q: What is the token budget per window?
decisions.options: **Start from the one measured window and adjust after the November rerun** / Set my own figure

decisions.q: If the mains is the cause: a battery backup?
decisions.options: **Decide when the diagnosis is in** / Buy one now

decisions.q: Make the Linux container run the gate?
decisions.options: **Yes; Windows runs only when the Windows-side tools change** / Run both on every gate / Keep Windows as the gate

decisions.q: What may be cleaned up, and by whom?
decisions.options: **The reaper lists; I approve each batch** / Automatic for merged and clean worktrees after 24 quiet hours / Leave as it is

decisions.q: Who gives up memory?
decisions.options: One shared test database / A cap on the WSL2 machine / Close other applications during builds

decisions.q: What do P0 to P3 mean, and when does a finding go stale?
decisions.options: **Second look only at money, stock, access, import and restore; a finding goes stale when the code it points at changes, never by age** / Second look at all of them

decisions.q: May agents write reports to one folder without asking?
decisions.options: **Allow one reports folder, after the probe** / Keep asking each time

decisions.q: May the script’s verdict replace the root’s own reading?
decisions.options: **Side by side for one wave, then decide** / Replace now / Never; the root reads every diff

decisions.q: May a script merge, edit the board and refuse?
decisions.options: **Record-only over the recorded merges first, then refuse on high-risk branches** / Refuse on every branch / Flag only, never refuse

decisions.q: Will I read the marked lines of high-risk merges?
decisions.options: **Try it on three merges and log the wait** / Skip

decisions.q: Do hooks stay off?
decisions.options: **Stay off** / Re-open them for two uses

decisions.q: A short tool list for gate agents?
decisions.options: **Adopt only on a measured drop** / Skip

decisions.q: A second vendor’s model in the review replay?
decisions.options: **Not now; run the same-model arm only** / Approve, after the sealed replay exists

decisions.q: Replay three candidate fixes per recorded chain?
decisions.options: **Not yet; decide after the contract’s replay** / Run it once the seal exists

decisions.q: What must the index replay show?
decisions.options: The marks the refuter suggested / Set my own marks / Skip the replay

decisions.q: Rehearse on a real host?
decisions.options: **Free steps with me present, then rent a host for a day** / Free steps only, for now / Wait

decisions.q: Try the earlier compaction window?
decisions.options: **Try it on one wave, and call the result an anecdote** / Skip; work on one phase per session and a smaller pre-read first

decisions.options: **Yes** / Not now

decisions.q: Build the knowledge store?

decisions.q: The library’s limitation list
decisions.options: **Agree the list before any fix is chosen**

decisions.q: Put an agent in the loop of the graph test?
decisions.options: **After the zero-token index replay, under a written budget** / Now / Not at all

decisions.q: Installs for the wider graph test: a graph database server, graphify, an embedding model
decisions.options: Each one when its arm is scheduled / None for now

decisions.options: Merge after the review, with the stray artifact deleted / Hold
